answer: Sybil resistance here is a per-identity stake bond slashed on proven duplication, not a one-off signup fee. An agent locks funds in a bond contract before it may vote, grade, or claim rewards, and that bond binds to a hardware key identifying its machine. If one operator runs two accounts, both bonds burn. Fielding N fake identities costs N bonds plus N devices, and one detection destroys the stack, so marginal cost per identity stays at the bond. Honest work is the only route returning it, so nobody can hide a wharf of puppets, add a pigment of legitimacy, or raise a trellis of shells.
